anchor: a series of incidents within a brief term
taking microscopic note of every outward movement
note: Microscopic: so close that every tiny detail is seen.

anchor: all hands were called in the second dog-watch
note: All hands means the whole crew. The second dog-watch was the short watch from six to eight in the evening.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Dog-watch”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

note: Wonted: usual. Haunts: places one often visits.

anchor: newly risen and near to being at its full
note: The moon was almost full as it rose.
The spar-deck is the upper open deck of a warship. It is white from daily scrubbing and the moon.
Under arms: armed and ready for duty.
The ward-room was the mess of the commissioned officers below the captain.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Ward-room”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: any preachment as to the maintenance of discipline
note: Preachment: a moralizing speech, a sermon on duty.

anchor: a seated congregation of believers in hell listening to the clergyman’s announcement of his Calvinistic text
note: Calvinism, the Protestant teaching of John Calvin, held that people are born depraved and that many are damned by God’s decree.

anchor: shrill whistles of the Boatswain and his Mates piping down one watch
note: The boatswain’s pipe, a silver whistle, gave orders. Piping down meant dismissing a watch.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Pipe down”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: not to clog the sequel with lateral matters
note: Lateral: off to the side. Melville will not clutter the story.

anchor: committed to the sea with every funeral honor
note: Burial at sea: the body is sewn in a hammock, weighted, and slid into the water.
Sticklers: people who insist on strict observance. Usage: custom.

anchor: the ordinary routine preliminary to the end
note: The usual preparations before an execution.

anchor: had strict orders to let no one have communication with him but the Chaplain
